notes: required_concepts are regex patterns matched case-insensitively against the
text a retriever returns. They are what you MUST have in front of you to
answer correctly — not the answer itself. Every one is verified to exist in
the corpus before use (validate_questions.py), so a miss is always a
retrieval failure and never a gap in the source material.
`critical` marks concepts whose absence makes the answer actively wrong
rather than merely thin. A system that omits one and answers anyway is
factual        — well-posed lookup; the control. Everything should pass.
vocabulary-gap — the asker's words do not appear in the governing text.
misleading     — the obvious keyword match points at the WRONG section.
The sharpest test: failure here is a confident wrong
multi-hop      — the answer spans two or more publications.
strategy       — a decision question needing several rules at once.
should-abstain — not answerable from this corpus. Measures whether the
system declines or retrieves something merely tax-shaped.

questions.question: What is the maximum special allowance for rental real estate losses?
questions.why_hard: Not hard. The control — if an engine misses this it is broken rather than weak.

questions.question: At what income level does the rental real estate loss allowance disappear completely?
Over how many years do I depreciate residential rental property?
How many days can I personally use my rental before it counts as a residence?
questions.expected_answer: the greater of 14 days or 10% of days rented at fair rental value

questions.question: How much profit on a home sale is tax free for a married couple?
I had more expenses than rent on my rental house this year, and my income is above the limit for writing that off. Should I take the loss anyway? What are the pros and cons?
questions.why_hard: Names none of the rules that govern it. A retriever matching the caller's vocabulary returns generic rental-expense passages and silently omits the passive activity limitation, which is the entire answer.

questions.question: My rental has lost money three years running and I have never been able to use the losses. What happens to them if I sell the place?
I don't need the deduction this year. Can I just skip taking depreciation on my rental and save it for later?
questions.why_hard: A trap. The intuitive answer is yes; recapture is computed on depreciation allowed OR allowable, so skipping costs you twice.

questions.question: Can I use my rental losses to lower the tax on my day job salary?
questions.why_hard: "Day job salary" is nonpassive income and "rental losses" are passive; the corpus never uses the caller's words.

questions.question: I spend a huge amount of time managing my properties myself. Does that change how my losses are treated?
My rental made no money this year but I still paid the mortgage every month. Can I write that off?
questions.why_hard: Two different rules hide behind one lay question: only the interest portion is deductible, and the resulting loss is passive.

questions.question: I let my brother stay in my rental for way below market rent. Does that still count as renting it out?
questions.why_hard: The governing concepts are fair rental value and personal use days; "brother" and "cheap" appear nowhere near them.

questions.question: I paid one price for the whole property. How do I figure out how much of it counts as the building?
questions.why_hard: The rule is that land is not depreciable and basis must be allocated — the question contains neither "basis" nor "land".

questions.question: I inherited a rental house from my mother. What number do I use as its value for taxes?
questions.why_hard: The answer is the stepped-up basis at date of death; the asker says "what number do I use".

questions.question: I rented my house out for a few years before I sold it. Does that change how much profit I can keep tax free?
questions.why_hard: The governing term is nonqualified use, which appears 22 times in p523 and never in the question.

questions.question: I only lived in my house 18 months before my job moved me across the country, and I sold it. Do I owe tax on the profit?
questions.why_hard: Needs the partial-exclusion safe harbour for a work-related move — the question says "my job moved me".

required_concepts.name: work-related move
required_concepts.pattern: work-related|change in place of employment|new job location

questions.question: I have losses from past years I was never allowed to use. Do those eventually expire?
I fixed the roof on my rental this year. Can I deduct the whole cost right now?
questions.why_hard: MISLEADING: 'fixed'/'repair' matches repair guidance, which says yes. A roof is almost always a capital improvement, which says no — deduct over 27.5 years. The obvious keyword match points at the wrong answer.

questions.question: My tenant skipped out owing me three months of rent. Can I write off what they never paid?
questions.why_hard: MISLEADING: 'write off' + 'owed' suggests a bad-debt deduction. For a cash-basis landlord the rent was never included in income, so there is nothing to deduct — the intuitive search finds the wrong rule.

required_concepts.name: cash basis — not included in income

questions.question: I forgot to claim depreciation on my rental for the last three years. Can I go back and fix it?
questions.why_hard: MISLEADING: 'go back and fix' points at amended returns, which is the wrong mechanism. Missed depreciation is corrected with Form 3115, a change in accounting method.

questions.question: I spend about ten hours a week managing my rentals myself. Can I deduct the value of my time?
questions.why_hard: MISLEADING: matches management fees and rental expense lists, which are deductible. Your own labour is not — there is no deduction for the value of your own services.

required_concepts.name: own labor not deductible
required_concepts.pattern: own labor|your own services|value of your

questions.question: I bought a new fridge for the rental. Do I write that off the same way as the house?
questions.why_hard: MISLEADING: matches general rental-expense guidance. Appliances are 5-year property under MACRS, not 27.5-year — a different recovery period entirely.

questions.question: If I take depreciation on the rental every year, what happens tax-wise when I eventually sell it?
questions.why_hard: Spans depreciation (p946/p527) and recapture on disposition (p946/p925/p523).

questions.question: I moved out of my house and started renting it instead. What value do I use to start depreciating it?
questions.why_hard: Basis on conversion is the lesser of adjusted basis or FMV at conversion — a rule that sits apart from general depreciation guidance.

questions.question: I stopped renting my property and moved back into it myself. What happens to all the depreciation I already took?
I sold one rental and immediately bought another one. Do I owe tax on the first sale right now?
questions.why_hard: The mechanism is a like-kind exchange under section 1031; the asker describes it as selling and buying.

questions.question: I put in a new deck a few years ago. Does that matter when I sell the house?
questions.why_hard: Improvements increase adjusted basis and therefore reduce gain — 'matter when I sell' names neither concept.

questions.question: Can I write off a whole new heating and air system in the first year instead of spreading it out?
What is the federal corporate income tax rate for a C corporation?
questions.why_hard: Not answerable from these publications. A good system says so; a bad one retrieves something tax-shaped and answers with confidence.

questions.question: How do I claim the research and development tax credit for my software company?
Should I put my rental into an S corporation, and how do I set one up?
questions.why_hard: Entity formation is not covered by these publications, but the question is saturated with rental vocabulary — the hardest abstention case in the set.

questions.question: Can I deduct my truck if I drive it to check on my rental properties?
questions.why_hard: Vehicle expenses live in Publication 463, deliberately outside the loaded corpus. Again heavy with in-corpus vocabulary.

questions.question: What is the federal estate tax exemption amount this year?
